messages:
Noah: quick sync - we need a lightweight internal comms template and a paired status-page snippet. goal: exact placeholders, clear cadence, and wording variants for 'no-customer-impact' vs 'partial' vs 'major'.

Elena: agree. my main ask: the first on-call notification (pager→Slack) should answer: what happened, who owns it, customer impact (yes/no + scope), and next update, all within 2 lines.

Ravi: drafting placeholders we should standardize: {{INC_ID}}, {{SEVERITY}}, {{SERVICE}}, {{SCOPE}}, {{SYMPTOM_PLAIN}}, {{TECH_SUMMARY}}, {{MITIGATION}}, {{OWNER}}, {{NEXT_UPDATE}}, {{STATUS_PAGE}}. Keep names uppercase so macros map cleanly.

incident-bot: incident created 1891004321. primary and secondary paged. Use `/incident update --id 1891004321` to post templated updates.

Noah: proposed internal Slack template (pasteable) - first post only: 
```
Noah ({{SEVERITY}}) — {{SERVICE}}: {{SYMPTOM_PLAIN}} ({{SCOPE}}).
Impact: {{SCOPE}} of customers affected. Owner: @{{OWNER}} | Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE}}.
Mitigation: {{MITIGATION}}
Links: {{STATUS_PAGE}} | runbook: {{RUNBOOK_LINK}}
Handoff: {{HANDOFF_SUMMARY}}
```
Keep first line < 120 chars. Use :red_circle: :large_orange_diamond: :white_check_mark: icons.

Elena: add a short "TL;DR for PMs/customer success" line for internal posts so wider teams can quickly copy a customer message. Example: `TL;DR: Some customers may see increased errors; engineers are investigating.`

comms-bot: suggestion — provide 3 customer-facing templates (initial, update, resolution). macros can substitute placeholders. Example initial (concise):
`We're investigating increased errors impacting some customers on {{SERVICE}}. We're actively working on a fix; updates at {{STATUS_PAGE}}.`

Ravi: and a slightly more detailed customer message when workaround is available: 
`Impact: certain API calls are returning 5xx. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff or use the standby endpoint at <url>. We expect a fix by {{NEXT_UPDATE}}.`

Noah: tone guidance — internal: factual, low drama, no root-cause speculation. customer: apologetic, constructive, include an action for customers if any. Avoid internal acronyms like "rfo" without explanation.

oncall-sre: on handoffs — require an explicit ack that includes 3 items: 1) I acknowledge (with timestamp), 2) checklist run (yes/no) with last checked logs/metrics, 3) hypothesis + immediate next action + next ETA. ack example: `oncall-sre: ack 16:12. ran runbook steps 1-3; saw leader flips in logs; restarting controller; next update 16:22.`

Elena: cadence rules proposal: severity=critical → updates every 15 min; severity=high → every 20 min; medium→ every 30-60 min. Customer-facing updates: initial within 30 min of confirming customer-visible impact, then hourly or on meaningful changes. Final resolution + follow-up postmortem within 72 hours.

incident-bot: cadence enforcement can be toggled per-incident. auto-reminder set for severity=critical at 15m. Bot will not auto-close without human confirmation.

Ravi: we should add short 'no impact' quick-close templates to avoid over-notifying. example internal quick close: 
`{{SEVERITY}} — Investigated: no customer impact found. Root cause: internal alert noise. Owner: @{{OWNER}}. Closing incident.`

Noah: debate point — how prescriptive should customer messages be about root cause pre-postmortem? my take: avoid RC speculation; use neutral phrasing like "cause under investigation" and promise follow-up.

Elena: +1. also add 'sensitive data check' boolean to the template to force a quick privacy review if any data exposure is suspected. placeholder: {{SENSITIVE_DATA_FLAG}} -> yes/no. If yes, trigger privacy oncall.

product-ops: UX ask — can the console show a "staging preview" of the customer copy when you push the status-page snippet? small modal with the three variants would help.

Ravi: action items: 1) I'll PR the canonical placeholder list and the three Slack/customer templates to /docs/incidents/comms-template.md. 2) Elena, can you draft the TL;DR copy examples for wider teams? 3) Noah, can you wire up the handoff ack wording into the runbook?

Elena: will do TL;DR examples. I'll include copy variants for: major outage, partial, and informational (no impact).

Noah: small automation note — ops wants a `/inc copy-to-status --variant initial` command that opens a pre-filled modal; product-ops to scope.

product-ops: ack, I'll scope ticket INC-914 for console preview + copy-to-status modal.

oncall-sre: runbook update note: require that the person taking over posts the last three commands run and last three log excerpts (or links) in the handoff if the incident is >30m. reduces wasted time.

Ravi: also adding a "comms tone guide" section: short bullets — 1) use plain language for customers, 2) be brief, 3) prioritize what customers can do, 4) apologize once, avoid repetitive apologies, 5) commit to an update time.

incident-bot: reminder: incident post-mortem template added to /docs/incidents/postmortem-template. Use it to populate the "customer follow-up" section.

Noah: final decisions captured: placeholders standardized, update cadence set, handoff ack required, bot won't auto-close. we'll iterate on wording variants. I'll assemble a 1-page cheat sheet and drop it in /docs/incidents by Thursday. please add comments on the PR.

Elena: thanks. tiny nudge — include one-liners PMs can paste into Zendesk for impacted customers. that will reduce noise.

Ravi: noted, adding Zendesk snippets to PR.

Noah: closing — thanks all. if you have edge-case phrasing (GDPR data, billing impact), add them to the PR review. :thumbsup:
